chunks: From him, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"There is no harm in a man selling slaves from Sind, Sudan, the Talid, the Jalib, and those born among the Bedouins."

Ibn Sinan said, and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said regarding a man who buys a boy or a girl, and he has a brother or sister or a mother in a city among the cities: "He should not take him from one city to another if he is young, and do not buy him. But if he has a mother, and she is pleased and he is pleased, then buy him if you wish."
ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for selling and relocating a slave child according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the marketability of slaves from specific regions like Sind and Sudan, reflecting the geographic trade networks of the era. It further establishes a nuanced legal principle regarding the relocation of a slave child, prioritizing the emotional well-being and consent of both the child and his mother to prevent familial separation or distress.
